A 53-year-old South Asian male visits his primary care provider due to a chronic cough that worsens at
night. He reports having this cough for several years, with worsening symptoms over the past few
months. He recently moved to the United States for construction work and has experienced a 10-pound
weight loss in the last 3 months. He also notes darker stools, which he attributes to a Western diet. He
denies difficulty swallowing, food getting stuck, or any family history of cancer. He drinks alcohol 1–2
times per week, has never smoked, and his vital signs are within normal limits: temperature 98.9°F
(37°C), blood pressure 108/78 mmHg, pulse 66/min, and respirations 15/min. Physical examination
reveals clear lungs bilaterally, a soft and non-distended abdomen, no tenderness to palpation, and
present bowel sounds. What is the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A)
Upper endoscopy (B) Barium swallow (C) Fecal occult blood test (D) 24-hour esophageal pH
monitoring (E) Abdominal ultrasound (F) Colonoscopy (G) CT scan of the chest and abdomen (H) Trial
of lansoprazole (I) Pulmonary function testing (J) Chest X-ray
 A. Upper endoscopy
B. Pulmonary function testing
C. Fecal occult blood test
D. Chest X-ray
E. Colonoscopy
F. Abdominal ultrasound
G. Trial of lansoprazole
